messages:
maya: Heads-up — getting multiple customer p95/p99 latency alerts in eu-west after last night's infra push. Started ~02:10 UTC.
simon: saw the alert, correlating now. any single tenant or widespread? :thinking:
nate: widespread across several queues, but strongest on embed-heavy routes. p99 up from ~450ms to 1.8s on eu-west-2.
maya: deploy-bot shows a scheduled firmware + host-kernel patch at 01:55 UTC rolled to canary then region-wide at 02:00. deploy-bot: canary success -> promote.
eng-sre-bot: linked metrics: host_iowait spike coincident with deploy, NVMe queue_depth increase, device_saturation on nodes hosting KV cache.
alice: possible storage contention. did we change qdisc or IO scheduler in the kernel patch? maya: yes the kernel bump enabled blk-mq rework + mq-deadline tuning by default.
nate: reproducing locally on a repro node — running a steady KV cache load with nvme-backed cache gives p95 spike after firmware upgrade.
simon: can we get a raw fio to reproduce on affected instances? share command we should run.
alice: run this on repro node:
```
fio --name=randread --rw=randread --bs=4k --size=10G --iodepth=32 --numjobs=4 --runtime=120 --time_based --direct=1 --filename=/dev/nvme0n1
```
maya: ran that, saw 20-30% higher latency and queue_depth skyrocketing during sustained load. kernel blk-mq config shows fewer hardware queues exposed after firmware change.
nate: hypothesis: firmware/kernel interplay reduced parallelism, causing per-request stalls; KV cache misses amplify IO bursts.
simon: mitigation ideas: 1) roll back kernel tweak or kernel package -> short term. 2) throttle background flushes / reduce iodepth on cache clients. 3) route heavy embed traffic to other regions while we triage.
maya: support-ops notified customers with ETA: "We're investigating increased API latencies in EU. Temporary mitigations underway, will update in 30m." :white_check_mark:
eng-sre-bot: action items created: #1 reproduce with fio (assigned nate); #2 node-level rollback plan (assigned simon); #3 traffic routing + canarying (assigned maya); #4 vendor support escalation (assigned alice).
simon: i'm preparing a rolling rollback playbook — can revert kernel package on a subset of nodes and canary for 15m. if rollback restores qdepth/latency we confirm the kernel interaction.
alice: opened ticket with HW vendor and attached nvme logs + dmesg + fio runs. asked for firmware microcode clarification.
nate: short-term workaround applied: lowered KV cache iodepth from 32 -> 8 and patched autoscaler to avoid bursty prefetches. p95 in eu-west dropped from 1.8s -> ~520ms but not fully back to baseline.
maya: good work. next steps: run driver bisect if rollback inconclusive, coordinate with vendor for firmware fix, and expand routing fallback to reduce customer impact until root cause fixed.
simon: rolling kernel rollback now on two canary hosts in eu-west-2. will watch latency and IO metrics for 30m.
maya: update in 18m: canary nodes back to baseline p99 and iowait reduced. rolling rollback proceeding cautiously. will post full postmortem template once stabilized.
alice: also note billing/ingress unaffected; no auth or API errors — purely infra perf regression.
support-ops: posting customer update: "We've rolled back a recent kernel change for a subset of hosts and seen meaningful latency improvement. We're performing a controlled rollback while we coordinate with our hardware vendor for a permanent fix." :loudspeaker:
eng-sre-bot: incident severity remains SEV2 until all regions verified. tagging on-call for follow-up.
maya: thanks everyone. keep threads short and paste any new logs here. if rollback doesn't hold we'll prepare to revert firmware via vendor instructions.
